title: Cornell notes
audience: For students who take notes in class but never get round to turning them into questions.
description: Your notes on the right, a question for each on the left, a short summary. Then your AI quizzes you.
tagline: Your notes, a cue for each, a summary.
note:
Cornell notes

Paste your lecture or reading notes into your AI. Your notes go on the right, a question each one answers on the left, and a short summary closes the section. To revise, cover the right column and answer the cues.

## Lectures
One section per lecture or chapter.

## Cues to revisit
The cues you missed when quizzed, ticked once you get them right.

prompt.default: Use my Pinto Notes note "Cornell notes". Read it with fetch before each change. When I paste or dictate notes from a lecture or a chapter, add a section at the end of "Lectures" with edit: a "###" heading with the topic and the date, then a table with two columns, Cue and Notes. Put my notes on the right as short rows in my own words, and on the left a question each row answers. End with a line starting "**Summary:**", two or three plain sentences. When I say "quiz me", ask me the cues one at a time without showing the notes. Add any I miss under "Cues to revisit" as a checklist, and tick one when I get it right later.

asks: Ask me for my lecture or reading notes, then make Cornell notes and quiz me.
Quiz me on supply and demand.
Which cues am I still missing?

args.old_string: One section per lecture or chapter.
args.new_string:
One section per lecture or chapter.
### Supply and demand, 5 November
| Cue | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| What shifts the demand curve? | Income, tastes, related goods' prices, expectations. |
| What moves along the curve? | Only a change in the good's own price. |
| What is the equilibrium price? | Where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. |
| What does a low price ceiling cause? | A shortage: people want more than sellers offer. |

**Summary:** Supply and demand meet at one price and quantity. Anything other than the price itself shifts a curve and moves that point; a price ceiling set too low leaves a shortage.

args.new_string:
The cues you missed when quizzed, ticked once you get them right.
- [ ] What shifts the demand curve?
- [x] What does a low price ceiling cause?
